scope: Existing observed Oudezijds39–71 row, 18 fronts over approximately100m. User-requested lighter roofline trim, stronger masonry and one optional shallow segmental-head style while preserving flat heads. No transfer or expansion acceptance.
decision: pass-bounded-offline-refinement-visual; actual-game/performance gate owned by root
method: Direct view_image review of four fixed municipal sources, final front/block/source-row images for all four fixed samples, opposite-obliques for the two curved-head areas, and matched prior-final front images for upper-unmatched, neck-middle and bell-lower plus cornice-upper block. Failure-seeking review of casing/glass contradictions, heavy trim, mortar noise and row composition. Tests are not visual acceptance.

criteria.reason: The selected brown fronts show a shallow continuous curved glass/casing silhouette; adjacent dark and pale fronts visibly retain straight heads. Curvature remains a local style rather than a uniform row treatment. No rectangular header crosses the curved apex in reviewed final views. Lower tall panes show a more conspicuous arch in the low-angle near view, but the row-scale result remains a slight rounded alternative rather than a separate broad arch family.

The formerly deep projecting cornice slabs read as appreciably thinner pale/dark bands. Cornice fronts remain capped with connected closure; no sky slit or floating slab is visible in the reviewed fronts/source-row views. Existing neck/bell/cornice mixture and neighboring heights remain recognizable against the prior-final comparison.

Brick courses and staggered vertical joints are more legible on brown/red fronts while dark fronts remain quiet. Mortar does not compete with pale surrounds or window grouping in the reviewed block/oblique views. Pale masonry remains the highest-contrast surface, already present in baseline; no new noisy checkerboard or row-wide washout appears. Game-distance readability requires root runtime evidence.

Frontage widths, pale trim cadence, tall lower/shorter upper window hierarchy, native narrow returns and roof-family variation remain in place. The two curved fronts add a bounded difference without overwhelming the retained flat majority. No new broad balcony or blank-return regression is visible.

preservedFailedEvidence.status: Initial failure reported by root: rectangular 3D optional header conflicted with curved painter. Final reviewed curved glass/casing no longer shows the conflicting bar. Preserve initial captures; do not rewrite them as accepted evidence.

worstReviewedView.reason: Strong low-angle near projection makes lower segmental heads the most rounded and highlights the flat treatment on the adjacent visible return. The curved glass and casing remain coherent; this is a selectable frontal style review, not exact photographed-building matching.

limits: This review does not certify per-address photographed window-head matching; sources remain predominantly flat-headed at the fixed central facades.
No new heldout or neighborhood transfer reviewed. The previously failed adjacent south compound-frontage remains outside acceptance.
Offline native stage omits game vegetation/vehicles/curated landmark meshes. Runtime modes, stationary desktop/touch camera pan, streaming and same-version performance must be reviewed separately.
Two of18 curved fronts and sixteen flat fronts are the root handoff inventory; this visual review verifies visible mixed treatment, not an independent catalogue count.
nextAction: Root personally inspect final comparisons and actual-game/performance evidence before marking this bounded refinement complete.
